title: Choose Your Tool
big_idea: Pick a tool, say why, and check your answer
child_idea: Many problems can be solved in more than one way. We pick a tool, say why we picked it, and check the answer another way.
skill: Choosing a method and checking it

moe.strand: Whole Numbers; Addition and Subtraction; Multiplication and Division; Money (Term 2 spiral, problem solving)
topics: Addition and subtraction within 100, more than and fewer than (Primary 1, Addition and Subtraction, p. 31)
Multiplication within 40 and division within 20: groups, sharing and the price of one (Primary 1, Multiplication and Division, p. 31)
Counting in 2s, 5s and 10s; odd and even numbers; positions in a line (Primary 1, Whole Numbers, p. 31)
Choosing and checking a method: problem-solving heuristics (draw a model, act it out, look for a pattern, make a list or table, work backwards)
moe.note: Strand label for the tutor only. A choose-the-tool consolidation lesson: it teaches no new idea. It spirals Term 2 in fresh numbers and asks the child to choose a tool (draw it, act it out, spot the pattern, list every way, make a table, work backwards), say why and check. It hosts Mi's Challenge Quest (20 minutes, minutes 35 to 55; a game with Mi, not a test); the tutor notes, the private notes sheet and the grown-up note are built from the quest block by tools/b_quest.py. Start here items are Primary 1 reach in fresh numbers (one or two steps, counting in 5s, the price of one, a missing number). BEYOND PRIMARY 1 ON PURPOSE and named: choosing a tool and giving a reason, and the same problem solved with a second tool (Think harder T1); counting places in a queue with both ends (T3); the numbers two counting lists share (T4); a three-step number puzzle reversed (G2); the price of one in two shops (G1); a picture equation with a sum and a product (G3). Non-routine types: queue counting, 'I think of a number' puzzles worked backwards, odd and even claims tested on examples, the price of one first, shapes as numbers. Owner decision, 22 Oct 2026: strong content with scaffolding, said plainly to families. Say this on the parent page and in the opening of the guide; do not describe the lesson as MOE-aligned or syllabus-aligned. Money is whole dollars only. Contest tag (tutor only): choose and justify a method, check by a second method.

Go further: three-step puzzles and the price of one in two shops, with no tool named.
Play Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi on private paper: 8 short gates and an optional secret cave. Under each gate the child circles the tool they used.

slides.subtitle: Pick a tool. Say why. Check.

mascot.say: Hi, I'm Mi. Let's notice, test and explain why!

slides.title: Warm-up: our toolbox

blocks.text: Six tools. Say each name with me.

head: Tool
What it is for
rows: Draw it: a picture or a strip
Spot the pattern: what repeats or grows
List every way: write each one
Make a table: rows and columns

slides.note: The toolbox page. Say the six names together, touching the tool cards on the kit page. Ask: which tool is for undoing the steps (work backwards); which is for writing each way (list every way); which uses counters (act it out). Children answer aloud or point. No writing, no marks. A child who joins cold needs nothing else: every tool is shown here with a picture. There is no wrong tool in this lesson.

slides.title: Try two tools

cols.head: DRAW IT
items: Ben has 6 marbles.
Kumar has 3 more than Ben.

slides.note: Two tools on tiny problems, about a minute each. Left: Ben has 6 marbles and Kumar has 3 more; draw a strip and count on: 9. Right: each bag has 3 sweets; a table adds 3 each row: 9 for 3 bags and 12 for 4 bags. Ask: how many marbles does Kumar have (9); how many sweets in 3 bags (9); in 4 bags (12). Children answer aloud or with fingers. A child who is unsure uses counters.

slides.title: Work backwards, and say why

blocks.head: I THINK OF A NUMBER
items: I add 3.
I get 10.
What is my number?

blocks.text: I will ... because ...

slides.note: Work backwards: undo the adding, so take 3 away from 10: 7. Check by going forwards: 7 + 3 = 10. Ask: what is my number (7); I think of a number, take away 2 and get 8: what is it (10). Then model the sentence frame once: I will work backwards because the story gives the end number. Children answer aloud. No writing.

slides.title: Sneak-peek puzzles

blocks.text: Ideas we have not met in this way. A guess is a great start. Nobody is judged.

cols.head: PUZZLE 1: anyone can try
items: Ravi is 3rd in a line.
Lily is 6th in the line.
How many children are between them?

cols.head: PUZZLE 2: think
items: Ben thinks of a number.
He doubles it and gets 14.
What is his number?

slides.note: Puzzle 1 (3rd and 6th; 2 children between) is an access question: a child can list 4th, 5th. Puzzle 2 is a thinking question: work backwards (half of 14 is 7). No tool is named in either: the two puzzles want different tools, and the Talk time slide comes back to them. Say: two sneak-peek puzzles; a guess is a great start; nobody is marked. Children write on their own paper. Nobody holds paper to the camera. There is no private chat. Answers: 2 children; 7. Do not reveal puzzle 2 until Talk time. Do not write scores or keep a list.

slides.title: Tool market: cards 1 and 2

blocks.text: Do not solve. Point to the tool you would start with.

cols.head: CARD 1
items: Ali has 15 stickers. Siti has 6 fewer. How many stickers does Siti have?

cols.head: CARD 2
items: Mei puts 20 counters into bags. Each bag has 4. How many bags?

slides.note: Tool market, about 3 minutes. Nobody solves. Read card 1 and card 2. Ask: which tool would you start with? Children point to a tool card on their own table, then volunteers say: I will ... because ... . Card 1 fits draw it (a strip). Card 2 has two good tools: act it out (deal counters into bags) or draw it. Say: there is no wrong tool; a good tool gets an answer you can check. Never call a child by name to answer.

slides.title: Tool market: cards 3 and 4

blocks.text: Do not solve. Point to the tool you would start with.

cols.head: CARD 3
items: Each box holds 5 pencils. How many pencils are in 7 boxes?

cols.head: CARD 4
items: Ben thinks of a number. He adds 6 and gets 15. What is his number?

slides.note: About 3 minutes. Nobody solves. Card 3 has two good tools: make a table (boxes and pencils) or spot the pattern (count in 5s). Card 4 fits work backwards (undo the adding). Ask: which tool would you start with, and why? Volunteers first; a pass is always fine.

slides.title: Tool market: cards 5 and 6

blocks.text: Do not solve. Point to the tool you would start with.

cols.head: CARD 5
items: Mei has 2 hats and 3 scarves. How many different hat and scarf pairs can she make?

cols.head: CARD 6
items: Is the sum of two odd numbers always even? Try some.

slides.note: About 2 minutes. Nobody solves. Card 5 fits list every way (write each pair); drawing also works. Card 6 fits spot the pattern: try some odd pairs and see what the sums do. Many answers are right. Ask for a reason each time: I will ... because ... .

slides.title: Two good tools

rows: Act it out or draw it
Make a table or spot the pattern

blocks.text: There is no wrong tool. Check your answer.

slides.note: About 2 minutes. Before showing the table, ask: which cards had more than one good tool? Children say. Then reveal: card 2 (act it out or draw it) and card 3 (make a table or spot the pattern). Say: when two tools work, pick the one you like, then check with the other if you have time. Answers are in the guide. Do not solve the cards.

slides.title: One problem, tool 1: draw it

blocks.head: PROBLEM
items: Ali saves $3 each week.
How many weeks to save $18?

slides.note: Tool 1: draw it. A strip for $18 cut into parts of $3. Count the parts: 6 weeks. Ask: how many parts (6). Whole dollars only. Children may use counters as $1.

slides.title: Tool 2: make a table

blocks.text: Which tool was quicker for you?

slides.note: Tool 2: make a table. Add $3 each row until $18: week 6. Ask: how many weeks (6). Then: which was quicker, the strip or the table? Volunteers first; there is no right answer. Some children prefer the strip, some the table.

slides.title: Check it a third way

blocks.head: WORK BACKWARDS
items: 6 weeks, $3 each week.
6 groups of $3 is $18.
It matches.

blocks.text: Put the answer back into the story.

slides.note: Check a third way: put 6 back into the story. 6 weeks at $3 a week is 6 groups of $3: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. It matches $18. Say: two tools gave 6, and putting 6 back agrees. That is how we know.

slides.title: When a tool gets stuck

blocks.head: BEN THINKS OF A NUMBER
items: He doubles it. Then he adds 2.
He gets 20.

blocks.text: Wait. Try a tool. Try a smaller case. Ask.

items: Guessing numbers is slow: it is stuck.
Try work backwards: 20 - 2 = 18.

slides.note: A tool that gets stuck. Children may try a guess first (try 5: 12; try 8: 18; slow). Say the stuck chant: Wait. Try a tool. Try a smaller case. Ask. Then switch to work backwards: 20 - 2 = 18, half of 18 is 9. Check forwards: 9 + 9 = 18, 18 + 2 = 20. Answer 9. The steps appear on the next slide, after the children have tried.

slides.title: Your turn

blocks.head: SITI THINKS OF A NUMBER
items: She adds 3. Then she doubles it.
She gets 16.

blocks.text: Choose a tool. Say why. Check.

slides.note: Each child works on their own paper. Siti adds 3, then doubles, and gets 16. Work backwards: half of 16 is 8, then 8 - 3 = 5. Check: 5 + 3 = 8, 8 + 8 = 16. Walk the cameras; do not ask children to hold papers up. Wait 10 seconds before helping. Answer: 5.

slides.title: Check: your turn
slides.note: Answer: 5. Read each step aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Children tick their own work with a tick. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

slides.title: Move and count

blocks.text: Count in twos. Stamp for each one.
Count in fives. Clap for each one.
Stand up. Sip some water.

slides.note: Four minutes. Stand up on camera. Count in twos to 20 and stamp softly on each number, then count in fives to 40 and clap on each number. No equipment, no running, a little clear space. A child may stay seated and tap the table. Do not give prizes or compare children. Then ask everyone to take out the closed Quest Log and a pencil, ready for Mi's Challenge Quest.

blocks.text: Questions 4 to 6. Take your time.

rows: The same problem with a second tool
Write a problem for a tool
Finish and check your own work

blocks.text: Everyone may choose. Not finished? Pages 3 to 5 are for home too.

slides.title: Talk and explain

blocks.head: MEI SAYS
items: Draw it is the best tool
for every problem.

blocks.text: Is Mei right? How could we check?
I think ... because ...

slides.note: One minute of talk to the grown-up next to you, or to your screen. Children try one problem two ways: 4 bags of 5 sweets by drawing and by counting in 5s. Then volunteers first; a pass is always fine; never call a child by name to answer. Model answer: no. Drawing is good for a whole and parts; a table is quicker for counting in 5s; work backwards is quicker for I think of a number. Repeat each child answer in your own words for the recording.

slides.title: Back to the sneak-peek

rows: List every way, or draw it

blocks.text: Many tools can work. Did you check?

slides.note: Reveal both puzzles. Puzzle 1: list the places 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th; the 4th and 5th are between: 2 children. Puzzle 2: half of 14 is 7; check 7 + 7 = 14. Do not read out anyone's earlier answer. Say: it was the same idea in both: pick a tool and check.

slides.title: Look-back
slides.note: Two minutes. Children tick or write the look-back box on page 5. A pass is always allowed. It is never graded, never collected in front of the group and never read out. This lesson is recorded so a friend who is away can catch up. The recording has me, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted. You may keep your microphone and camera off.
Start the recording now. Do not use children's first names on the recording.
@rec
Microphone off until I ask you to speak. To answer, say it with me on three, show fingers, or give a thumbs up. Nobody holds paper up to the camera.

start.text: Ben is 6th in a queue. Lily is 9th in the same queue. Fill in the blanks.

start.text: Each child thinks of a number. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: 20 sweets in bags of 4 make [] bags.

start.hint: Count on in 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, then one more.

think.text: Ben saves $3 each week. He wants to save $15. Use two tools. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: Make a table. Ben needs [] weeks.

Which was quicker for you? Circle one.

think.text: Mei thinks of a number. She doubles it. Then she adds 3. She gets 17. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: Check going forwards. Double her number: [2]. Then add 3: [2].

think.hint: Undo the last step first. Take 3 away from 17.

think.solution: The places are 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th: 6 children. 9 - 4 = 5 leaves out Lily, so Ben is not correct.

think.text: Mei counts in 3s: 3, 6, 9, and so on. Ravi counts in 4s: 4, 8, 12, and so on. Fill in the blanks.

parts.text: The first number that both say is [2].
The next number that both say is [2].

investigation.title: Write a problem for a tool

menu.title: Is there another tool?
menu.tutor: Mei counted 4 bags of 5 sweets by drawing. Is there another tool that would work? Try counting in 5s, or a table. Which was quicker?
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Mei drew 4 bags of 5 sweets. Find another tool that works. Which is quicker?
menu.answer: Counting in 5s (spot the pattern) gives 5, 10, 15, 20. A table of bags and sweets gives the same 20. Drawing works too. Any tool that gets 20 and can be checked is a good tool.

menu.title: Make a tool problem for your grown-up

menu.answer: No single answer. Check with the tool named: for example, 'I think of a number and add 5 to get 12' works well backwards (12 - 5 = 7).

menu.title: Teach it back
menu.tutor: Pretend a toy has never worked backwards. Show it how to find the number: I think of a number, add 3 and get 10.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Show a grown-up how to work backwards when a number plus 3 is 10.

parent.summary: This was a choose-the-tool lesson: nothing new was taught. We met six tools (draw it, act it out, spot the pattern, list every way, make a table, work backwards), solved mixed problems from the term in fresh numbers, picked a tool, said why and checked the answer another way. Most questions are Primary 1 work; choosing a tool and giving a reason, queue counting with both ends, three-step number puzzles and the price of one in two shops go past the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. questions.skill: A place in a queue and how many are in front (Term 2 Lesson 1); a strip for fewer (Term 2 Lesson 2)
questions.text: Kumar is 6th in a line. Ben has 24 marbles. Jenny has 8 fewer marbles than Ben.

parts.text: There are [box] children in front of Kumar.

questions.say: Gate 1. Kumar is 6th in a line. Ben has 24 marbles. Jenny has 8 fewer marbles than Ben. Part a: how many children are in front of Kumar? Part b: Jenny has blank marbles.
questions.solution: In front of the 6th child are the 1st to the 5th: 5 children. Jenny has fewer, so take away: 24 - 8 = 16.

questions.skill: A hidden number in a picture equation, and checking a friend's number (Term 2 Lesson 3)
questions.text: Each shape is a number. The star + the star + the star = 18. Ben says the star is 5.

parts.text: Is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No. [yesno]

questions.say: Gate 2. Each shape is a number. The star plus the star plus the star equals 18. Ben says the star is 5. Part a: is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No. Part b: the star is blank.
questions.solution: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, not 18, so Ben is not correct. 6 + 6 + 6 = 18, so the star is 6.
mistakes: (a) Yes (not putting 5 back into the line).

questions.skill: Odd and even (Term 2 Lesson 4) and counting in 5s (Term 2 Lesson 6)
questions.text: Mei adds 9 and 7. Siti counts in 5s.
questions.say: Gate 3. Mei adds 9 and 7. Siti counts in 5s. Part a: write odd or even. 9 plus 7 is blank. Part b: count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, blank, 25.
questions.solution: 9 + 7 = 16, and 16 pairs up with none left over, so it is even. Counting in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.

questions.skill: Groups of the same size and the times sign (Term 2 Lesson 5); sharing equally (Term 2 Lesson 7)
questions.text: Jenny has 4 plates. Each plate has 6 cookies. Siti shares 18 sweets equally among 3 friends.
questions.say: Gate 4. Jenny has 4 plates. Each plate has 6 cookies. Siti shares 18 sweets equally among 3 friends. Part a: fill in the boxes: blank times blank equals blank. Part b: each friend gets blank sweets.
questions.solution: 4 groups of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, so 4 × 6 = 24 (6 × 4 = 24 is also right). 18 shared equally among 3 friends is 6 each.
questions.right: Both correct (4 and 6 in either order, and 24).
questions.partly: One of the two correct, or the product right with the factors swapped or missing.

questions.skill: A times story with a second step (Term 2 Lesson 8)
questions.text: Ali has 4 boxes. Each box has 5 pencils. He gives 7 pencils to Ben.
questions.say: Gate 5. Ali has 4 boxes. Each box has 5 pencils. He gives 7 pencils to Ben. Part a: the boxes have blank pencils. Part b: Ali has blank pencils left.
questions.solution: 4 groups of 5 is 20 pencils. He gives 7 away: 20 - 7 = 13.
questions.partly: Part a right and part b wrong (for example 27), or part b right from a wrong part a.

questions.skill: Find one first, then many (Term 2 Lesson 9)
questions.say: Gate 6. 4 cups cost 16 dollars. Part a: 1 cup costs blank dollars. Part b: 5 cups cost blank dollars.
questions.solution: $16 shared equally among 4 cups is $4 each. 5 cups cost 5 groups of $4, which is $20.
questions.partly: Part a right and part b wrong, or part b right from a wrong part a.

questions.skill: A number puzzle with two steps, and checking a friend's number
questions.text: Mei thinks of a number. She doubles it and then adds 5. She gets 21. Ben says her number is 9.

parts.text: Is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No. [yesno]

questions.say: Gate 7. Mei thinks of a number. She doubles it and then adds 5. She gets 21. Ben says her number is 9. Part a: Mei's number is blank. Part b: is Ben correct? Circle Yes or No.
questions.solution: 21 - 5 = 16 and half of 16 is 8. Check: 8 + 8 = 16, 16 + 5 = 21. Ben's 9 gives 9 + 9 + 5 = 23, not 21, so Ben is not correct.

questions.skill: Every way, and a skip-count pattern
questions.text: Siti has 2 hats and 3 scarves. She wears one hat and one scarf. The shop counts pens in 4s.
questions.say: Gate 8. Siti has 2 hats and 3 scarves. She wears one hat and one scarf. The shop counts pens in 4s. Part a: she can dress blank different ways. Part b: count in 4s: 4, 8, 12, blank, 20.
questions.solution: Each hat goes with each of the 3 scarves: 3 + 3 = 6 ways. Counting in 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20.

optional.skill: Queue counting with both ends, and checking a claim
optional.text: Think harder (optional). Ravi is 7th from the front and 4th from the back of a line. Mei says there are 11 children in the line.

parts.text: Is Mei correct? Circle Yes or No. [yesno]
There are ___ children in the line.

optional.say: The secret cave has one more puzzle, and it is optional. You may skip it. Ravi is 7th from the front and 4th from the back of a line. Mei says there are 11 children in the line. Is Mei correct? Circle Yes or No. Then write how many children are in the line. Choose a tool, and write why you chose it.
optional.answer: No; 10 children (6 in front of Ravi, Ravi, and 3 behind him)
optional.solution: There are 6 children in front of Ravi and 3 behind him, and Ravi himself: 6 + 1 + 3 = 10. 7 + 4 = 11 counts Ravi twice.
optional.note: Never marked and never counted. Whether the child tried it adds one neutral phrase to the line for the grown-up; a skipped cave adds nothing.

give: A week before: send the grown-up note (L20_Quest_Parent_Note.pdf) and the Quest Log (L20_Quest_Log.pdf, 4 pages) with the lesson materials. Families print the Quest Log at 100%, keep it closed in an envelope and find a quest partner (a grown-up or a brother or sister). A family with no printer tells you: arrange another way (for example the make-up slot).

Tell the group in the opening and at slide s-quest1: this is Mi's Challenge Quest, a game with Mi. Everyone works on their own paper with a quest partner beside them. Under each gate they circle the tool they used and tick I checked: there is no wrong tool. It is not a race, a gate may be skipped, and nothing is shown to the group.

Start at minute 35 (straight after the brain break) and finish by minute 55. Children open the Quest Log only when you say. The paper lies flat on the table and is never held up. The quest partner may talk about how to start and ask 'how do you know?', but does not give answers. Cameras may be on or off. Use your own watch out of sight of the camera: no clock, countdown or timer is ever shown to the children.

Read each page aloud, one gate at a time (the script has the words), then leave quiet working time: about 2.5 minutes for each page of two gates, and 4 for page 4. After each page say that the gates are open and Mi swims on, whatever the answers. Say nothing about right or wrong, and read no answers. A middle child needs about 17 minutes in all; a slower child may finish in the first minutes of the workbook.

Allowed: fingers, counters and talk with the quest partner. Not allowed: a calculator, a grown-up giving answers, looking at the workbook. A child who finishes early turns the Quest Log over and draws quietly.

After page 2, take a one-minute stretch (stand, shake out, sip water). After page 4, show slide s-quest2. Do not collect or look at any Quest Log. While children work, notice (do not write on the shared screen) how they start: counters, drawing, a table, talking to the partner, and which tool they circle.
after: Same day: the grown-up takes ONE clear photo of each of the 4 pages (page flat, taken straight from above, the whole page in view, and the name on each page) and sends them to the program's business WhatsApp, +65 9880 5962, and to no other number. Never to a child, never to a personal phone, never into the class chat.

Within 3 days: open the photos only on the business WhatsApp (never on a personal phone) and write your private notes (section 5) for each child, from the photos and what you saw on camera. Section 4 shows what each answer tells you; accept either order of 4 and 6 in gate 4. Nothing is written on the child's paper, nothing is added up and no order of children is made. Nothing about the quest goes back to the child or the group except thanks.

Write ONE line for each grown-up from your notes (section 7): what we saw, in plain words, and one small next step if it helps. It is sent to the parent only. No marks, no x out of 8, no ranking, no comparison with other children, no prediction.

Fill in the group advice sheet (section 6): what several children were still working on, with no names, and what you will do in the first lessons of next term. It is kept for next term's tutor and is never shown to families.

Once the line is sent, save the photos to the program's private file store and delete them from the business WhatsApp chat. The program keeps the photos for 90 days after the program ends, then deletes them, as the privacy notice says. Delete each child's notes sheet when the line is sent (keep only the line in the family file, and the group advice sheet). Never forward the photos or save them to a personal phone or any other device.
At the start of next term say to the whole group: thank you for playing Mi's Challenge Quest; there is nothing to share and nothing to fear. Never name a child or an answer.
late: A child who was away or whose family prefers another time: plays the quest at the make-up slot BEFORE watching the recording (the quest is not on the recording, so no gate is given away). It is a small group or a pair with Mi, with a parent beside the child on camera. The tutor never sits alone with one child on a private call.

A child who joined late: the family may choose to leave out gates for lessons the child did not attend. Write nothing for those gates; if no gate of an area was taught, the line for the grown-up says nothing about that area.
A family that does not want the quest: no problem. The child does the Term 2 Lesson 10 work as usual and the line for the grown-up uses your own notes from the lessons only.
A child who is upset or stuck: remind the group (open session) that every gate can be skipped and Mi swims round it. Do not single the child out. The grown-up may stop the quest at any time.

A family with no printer: tell the family to say so a week before and arrange another way (for example the make-up slot, with the Quest Log sent to the family another way). Never ask a child about it in front of the group.
privacy_checklist: Quest Logs are never held up to the camera and never read out.
No answer is said aloud during or after the quest. Gates open for everyone, whatever the answers.
No clock, countdown or timer is shown; nobody is told who finished first or last.

Photos come to the program's business WhatsApp (+65 9880 5962) only; tutors never use a personal phone; photos are kept 90 days after the program ends, then deleted; the line goes to the parent only; no private message to any child.

No score, no x out of 8, no ranking, no comparison between children, and no tally or count of any kind on a child's page or anywhere a family can see. In your own notes: words only. You may circle one of the three words (with help / with a prompt / on their own) for each habit in the private notes sheet (section 5); never add the circles up, never compare children, and never say or show the words to a child or a grown-up.

The recording captures the tutor, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted: the recording is paused for the whole quest (slides s-quest1 and s-quest2) and restarted for the workbook. The WhatsApp number is never on a slide.
